rows.rewrite: net billing cost responsibility meter interconnection distributed generation facility
rows.answer:
The Distributed Generator must bear all costs for the interconnection facilities up to the interconnection point, including the installation of meters [ S3 ][ S5 ]. These rules are from the repealed Net Metering Regulations [ REPEALED ]; however, they continue to apply to licences and agreements that were executed under those regulations according to the savings clause in the Prosumer Regulations [ S6 ].

[S3] Net Metering Regs 2015, reg. 12(1), p. 7 (repealed)
[S5] Net Metering Regs 2015, reg. 12(3), p. 7 (repealed)
[S6] Prosumer Regs 2026, reg. 21(2), p. 7

rows.rewrite: bidirectional meter requirement for distributed generation facility net billing prosumer detection bill
rows.answer:
A solar connection must use either a standard meter that can register electricity flow in two directions, or two separate meters – one for selling electricity to the licensee and one for purchasing electricity from the licensee [S2]. The earlier Net Metering Regulations also required equipment to measure flow in both directions, but those rules have been repealed; they still apply only to existing agreements covered by the savings clause in the Prosumer Regulations 2026, which states billing will be according to the national average power purchase price and later the national average energy purchase price [S5][S6].

[S2] Prosumer Regs 2026, reg. 5(1), p. 4
[S5] Net Metering Regs 2015, reg. 13(1), p. 7 (repealed)
[S6] Prosumer Regs 2026, reg. 21(2), p. 7

drafts.text: Yes, a solar (distributed generation) connection must use a meter that can register electricity flowing in both directions, or alternatively two separate meters – one for electricity sold to the licensee and one for electricity purchased from the licensee [S2]. The earlier Net Metering Regulations also required equipment to measure flow in two directions, but those rules have been repealed; they still apply only to existing agreements covered by the savings clause in the Prosumer Regulations 2026 [S5][S6].

rows.rewrite: old net metering export tariff fuel adjustment taxes included
rows.answer:
The repealed Net‑Metering Regulations 2015 required the Distribution Company to pay only the off‑peak rate of the consumer’s category for exported units, and it did not include fuel‑price adjustment, duties or other levies [S1]. This old (repealed) rule still applies to existing agreements, and under the savings clause the billing is to be done at the national average power purchase price until the agreement expires, after which the national average energy purchase price applies for renewals [S6].

[S1] Net Metering Regs 2015, reg. 14(4), p. 7 (repealed)
[S6] Prosumer Regs 2026, reg. 21(2), p. 7

drafts.text: Under the repealed Net‑Metering Regulations 2015, the Distribution Company paid only the off‑peak rate of the consumer’s category for exported units; other charges such as fuel‑price adjustment and duties/levies were not payable by the DISCO [S1]. This is the old (repealed) rule, which still applies to existing agreements according to the savings clause in the Prosumer Regulations 2026 [S6].

rows.rewrite: maximum duration of detection bill coverage months for electricity theft
rows.answer:
The maximum period that a detection bill can cover is twelve months for unregistered consumers and up to six months for registered consumers [S1]. However, for general‑supply consumers the period is further limited to three billing cycles [S2].

[S1] Consumer Service Manual 2025, clause 9.1.3, p. 61
[S2] Consumer Service Manual 2025, clause 9.2.3, p. 63

rows.rewrite: avoid late payment surcharge billing cycle payment deadline DISCO
rows.answer:
To avoid the Late Payment Surcharge, pay the bill on or before the due date [S1]. If paying by cheque, pay order or bank draft, deposit it at the Revenue Office and the bank branch at least three days before the due date so it is realized by the due date [S1]. A surcharge will also not be imposed if the due date is officially extended [S2].

[S1] Consumer Service Manual 2025, clause 6.7.2, p. 50
[S2] Consumer Service Manual 2025, clause 6.8.1, p. 50

rows.rewrite: late meter reading extended billing cycle unit charge calculation detection bill
rows.answer:
When the billing cycle extends beyond the normal month, the units are calculated on a pro‑rata basis [S1]. For example, if a Lifeline consumer’s meter shows 54 units for 33 days, the calculation is 54 ÷ 33 × 30 = 49 units, which are billed as Lifeline units for that month; any units above the Lifeline threshold are carried forward to the next billing cycle [S1].

[S1] Consumer Service Manual 2025, clause 6.1.1.1, p. 45

drafts.text: When the billing cycle extends beyond the normal month, the units are calculated on a pro‑rata basis. The actual units recorded are divided by the number of days the reading covers and then multiplied by 30 days (the length of a calendar month). For example, if a Lifeline consumer’s meter shows 54 units for 33 days, the calculation is 54 ÷ 33 × 30 = 49 units, which are billed as Lifeline units for that month; any units above the Lifeline threshold are carried forward to the next billing cycle [S1].

rows.rewrite: exceeding sanctioned load actions by DISCO load increase penalty billing cycle
rows.answer:
If a consumer uses load above the sanctioned load, DISCO shall issue a notice to the consumer to apply for extension of load within fifteen days of receipt of the notice [S2]. The consumer must apply for the extension and complete the required formalities; otherwise DISCO shall disconnect the power supply [S2][S4]. DISCO shall also immediately change the tariff to a higher category (for example, from B‑1 to B‑2) and recover the difference of charges for the period of misuse, but the retroactive recovery shall not exceed six months [S1]. The failure to apply for load extension is listed as a ground for disconnection [S4].

[S2] Consumer Service Manual 2025, clause 8.2.10, p. 55
[S4] Consumer Service Manual 2025, clause 8.1, p. 54
[S1] Consumer Service Manual 2025, clause 7.5.2, p. 52
